prompt:
Paint ONE place into this tile of a painted grand-strategy map. The input is the finished map around the place, seen straight down; the place stands at the exact CENTRE of the image.

The place: Thiên Xu Tông, great seat. Paint it as a great sect's seat: vertical, stacked pagoda roofs and terraces climbing the slope, the tallest outline in the land, walls and gates, a main hall.
How it looks: High on a bare mountain above the heart of the continent, seven terraced halls step down a curving ridge in the bent line of the Northern Dipper, each a little lower than the last. The first and highest, the Pivot Hall, carries a slender black-iron spire that catches the last light long after the valleys are dark. Around the seat the slopes are strangely green for such a height, the mark of the Bắc Thần Phúc Địa.
Art brief: The tallest vertical in the heart: a high bare grey mountain whose curving ridge carries seven stepped terraces in a bent line, each with grey-blue stone halls under dark slate pagoda roofs, the highest terrace bearing a stacked three-roof hall topped by a thin black-iron spire. Unusually green slopes and pines around the terraces against the grey rock of the peak, a switchback road climbing from the lower left. Warm golden light from the top left lighting the spire tip and the west faces of the terraces. No text, no people larger than specks, nothing outside the place's footprint.

Rules:
- Paint the place as a small, finely detailed miniature, as if a model-maker had built it into this painted relief: seen from above at a gentle angle so roofs, walls and towers read clearly, its base sitting naturally on the terrain that is there (follow the slopes, the shore, the river).
- Keep it centred and compact: the whole place fits inside a circle about 25 % of the image width across the centre. Short roads or paths may lead out of it.
- Match the map exactly: the same golden-hour light from the TOP LEFT with soft shadows to the bottom right, the same painterly style, colours and level of detail as the surrounding terrain; the building scale fits the trees and hills around it.
- Leave everything outside that central circle exactly as it is in the input.
- Never: text, labels, banners with writing, flags with symbols, people larger than specks, a frame, a vignette, clouds over the place.
